Requirements: Admission to the university is a separate administrative process governed by the university’s Office of Admissions. For admission requirements, deadlines and instructions, please see Undergraduate Admission under the Admissions section of this catalog or visit the website for the Office of Admissions. This program is designed for students who are highly motivated to earn a bachelor's degree but have some college credit, or extensive experience (such as military or vocational training), and have been unsuccessful in achieving a bachelor's degree.

A minor in applied gerontology is available to all undergraduate students. Students must complete 18 semester hours of course work, with a minimum of 9 hours at the advanced level. A minimum GPA of 2.5 is required on all courses counted toward the minor. A minimum grade of C is required for all minor courses. Students must complete: ADSU 3000, ADSU 3010, ADSU 4100. Admission to the university is a separate process from admission to the College of Visual Arts and Design. Consult the Admission section of the catalog for more information. Admission to CVAD B.A. and B.F.A. Programs: Freshmen must be admitted to the university. Transfer students must be admitted to the university. CVAD requirements for admission for freshmen and transfer students are listed below. Freshmen: Must have a high school cumulative GPA of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale. Transfer students: Must have completed 12 or more transferable hours, have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale (including all transfer work), and be in good standing at the last institution attended. Admission to the university and the CVAD undergraduate program does not guarantee admission into a particular undergraduate major within the college. To be considered for admission as a first-time in college student, applicants must be a graduate of an accredited high school or possess a GED certificate, meet the Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP) requirements (completion of the Foundation, Recommended, or Distinguished high school program), and submit official transcripts from all high school(s) attended. Applicants must submit official test scores from the SAT or ACT; however, a test-optional pathway is available for eligible applicants.

Complete 45 semester hours of college coursework, including the UNT core courses, with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.75. Complete all pre-major course requirements (ASLP 1040, BIOL 1710, BIOL 1720, PSYC 1630, TECM 2700) with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.75. ASLP 1040 and PSYC 1630 must be completed with a minimum grade of C or better. Achieve a minimum grade of C or better in all pre-major courses (ASLP 1040, BIOL 1710, BIOL 1720, PSYC 1630, TECM 2700) and other courses taken for the major.

Students must meet the admission requirements for the College of Engineering. All students must meet university admission requirements. In addition to university requirements, the College of Engineering has specific academic requirements for unconditional admission directly into a major. For assured admission, freshmen entering the College of Engineering must meet the same academic qualifications as listed in the general Undergraduate Admission section of the catalog, but with higher math readiness. Freshmen must be calculus ready to be admitted into an engineering major. Calculus ready means eligible to enroll in MATH 1710 Calculus I (C or better in MATH 1650 Pre-Calculus or MATH 1600 Elementary Probability and Statistics, or MATH 1710 placement test).

First-time freshmen are students who have earned a high school diploma (or GED) and who have completed fewer than 12 college credit hours after high school graduation.

Applying for Admission:
Apply online using the ApplyTexas Application at goapplytexas.org or the Common App at commonapp.org.
Send Official High School Transcript
Send Official ACT/SAT Scores (UNT ACT school code 4240, UNT SAT school code 6481)

Automatic Admission:
Freshmen are automatically admitted to UNT if they meet one of the following requirements:
Beginning Fall 2023, students in the top 10% of their graduating class will be automatically admitted to UNT.
Beginning Fall 2023, students graduating in the top 25% of their class who have an SAT score of 1030 (Math + Critical Reading) or an ACT composite of 20 or higher will be automatically admitted to UNT.
Beginning Fall 2023, students graduating in the top 50% of their class who have an SAT score of 1130 (Math + Critical Reading) or an ACT composite of 23 or higher will be automatically admitted to UNT.
Beginning Fall 2023, students graduating in the third quartile (50.1-75%) of their class who have an SAT score of 1230 (Math + Critical Reading) or an ACT composite of 26 or higher will be automatically admitted to UNT.

Individual Review:
Applicants who do not meet the above automatic admission requirements will be reviewed individually for admission. Applicants for individual review are generally strong students who may not meet automatic admission requirements. When conducting an individual review, the Admissions Office considers a number of factors, including high school courses and grades, SAT/ACT scores, essays, extracurricular activities, leadership positions, community service, work experience, special talents, and other factors.

You may be admitted to UNT as an entering freshman if you meet ONE of the following requirements: 1. Assured Admission: Rank in the top 25% of your high school class AND satisfy the Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP); OR have an SAT score of 1200 or higher (combined Critical Reading and Math scores) or an ACT composite score of 26 or higher AND satisfy the Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP). 2. Individual Review: If you don't meet the assured admission requirements, your application will be reviewed individually. To be considered for individual review, you must: Rank in the top 50% of your high school class AND satisfy the Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP); OR have an SAT score of 1030 or higher (combined Critical Reading and Math scores) or an ACT composite score of 20 or higher AND satisfy the Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP); AND have a minimum of a 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale. Additional items such as essays, letters of recommendation, and a resume may be requested. SAT or ACT scores are required for freshman applicants unless specifically stated otherwise for certain waivers.

All students officially admitted to the university will be admitted to the College of Engineering and will be advised by the college staff. During the first two years, students in the Biomedical Engineering program follow a common pre-professional curriculum. Students formally apply for admission to the professional program within the department after successful completion of the pre-professional curriculum.
Admission to the professional program requires completion of at least 30 semester hours of course work applicable to the biomedical engineering degree with a minimum 2.5 GPA in all math, science and engineering courses taken at UNT and a minimum 2.5 overall GPA in all courses taken at UNT. Transfer students with 30 or more hours must also meet these requirements based on all courses taken at UNT. All students must complete ENGR 1304, PHYS 1710/1730, CHEM 1410/1430, MATH 1710, MATH 1720, and ENGR 2304 with a minimum grade of C.
Students must meet with their academic advisor to formally apply to the professional program.

A minor in Business Analytics for non-business majors is awarded to students who complete 18 hours in approved courses. Minor Requirements: Minimum 2.0 GPA in minor courses. Minimum 2.0 GPA in all courses completed at UNT. Must have completed 60 hours. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. None of the minor courses may be taken pass/no pass. Students must complete the statistics prerequisite with a C or better prior to enrolling in BANA 3000.

Admission to the university is the first step toward becoming a student at UNT. Detailed information is available at https://admissions.unt.edu/apply. In addition to satisfying university admission requirements, students must meet minimum requirements to be admitted to the G. Brint Ryan College of Business as a business major. To declare a business major, students must meet the following requirements: Be in good standing with the university; Have completed a minimum of 45 semester credit hours; Have completed the following courses with a minimum grade of C in each: ACCT 2010/2020, BCIS 2610, ECON 1100/1110, DSCI 2710/2810, MATH 1190/1321, and ENGL 1310/1320; Have a minimum 2.7 cumulative GPA on all college credit hours attempted.
Must have a minimum 2.0 UNT GPA.

A minimum of 18 semester hours in Chinese courses, including CHIN 1010, CHIN 1020, CHIN 2040, CHIN 2050, and 6 advanced semester hours selected from CHIN 3010, CHIN 3020, CHIN 3030, CHIN 3040, CHIN 3050, CHIN 3060, CHIN 3070, CHIN 3080, CHIN 3090, CHIN 3091, CHIN 3092, CHIN 3093, CHIN 3094, CHIN 3095, CHIN 3096, CHIN 3097, CHIN 4010, CHIN 4020, CHIN 4040, CHIN 4050, CHIN 4060, CHIN 4070. Admission to the BFA in Communication Design is a competitive process and is based on performance in foundation-level visual arts and design courses, submission of a portfolio of work, and academic performance. Students interested in applying to the BFA in Communication Design must first be admitted to the University of North Texas. Students apply to the BFA in Communication Design upon successful completion of the Foundation Year (ART 1301, ART 1302, ART 1303, ART 1304, ART 1305, ART 1306, ART 1307 and ART 1308), and ART 2307 and ART 2308. Students must earn a grade of B or better in each of the following courses: ART 1302, ART 1303, ART 1304, ART 1305, ART 2307 and ART 2308, and maintain a minimum 2.75 GPA. UNT is test-optional for students applying for fall 2024 and beyond. If you choose not to submit test scores, we’ll make an admission decision based on your high school GPA and class rank, if available. Some students who choose not to submit test scores may be required to participate in an admission interview. If you choose to submit test scores, they can be used in your admission review process if they meet our requirements or can be considered for scholarship eligibility. UNT also uses the Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP) which states that all students are eligible for automatic admission if they graduate in the top 10% of their high school class. The required documents for freshman applicants are: Application for admission (ApplyTexas or Common App), Official high school transcript, Official SAT or ACT scores (Optional for Fall 2024 and beyond), Application fee or fee waiver.

Students interested in declaring a major in Computer Science or Information Technology must meet the general undergraduate admission requirements for the university. Admission to the university is based on the strength of academic preparation and performance in high school. A freshman applicant is eligible for admission if they meet the general admission requirements. Automatic Admission criteria include: top 10% class rank, OR a minimum of 1030 on the SAT (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing + Math) with at least a 500 in Evidence-Based Reading and Writing, OR a minimum composite score of 20 on the ACT with at least a 16 on the English and Math sections. Applicants not meeting automatic admission criteria will be individually reviewed based on high school coursework, essay, and extracurricular activities, as well as test scores and class rank. Official high school transcripts and SAT or ACT scores are required for all freshmen. Essay, resume, and letters of recommendation are optional and will be reviewed if submitted.

Requirements:
General Admission Requirements
Freshman applicants must be graduates of an accredited high school or must have completed the equivalent of a high school education in an approved setting. All freshman applicants are required to submit an official high school transcript, official SAT or ACT scores, and a completed application for admission. Homeschool transcripts must be accompanied by an approved homeschool diploma or certification of completion.

The university reserves the right to deny admission to any applicant if, in the judgment of the university, the applicant is not an acceptable candidate for admission.

Assured Admission Policy
A freshman applicant will be admitted to the university if they meet the following assured admission requirements:

Rank in the top 25 percent of their high school graduating class AND submit an ACT composite score of 20 or an SAT total score of 1030 (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing + Math).
Rank in the second quarter (26-50 percent) of their high school graduating class AND submit an ACT composite score of 23 or an SAT total score of 1130 (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing + Math).
Rank in the third quarter (51-75 percent) of their high school graduating class AND submit an ACT composite score of 26 or an SAT total score of 1240 (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing + Math).
Rank in the fourth quarter (76-100 percent) of their high school graduating class AND submit an ACT composite score of 29 or an SAT total score of 1360 (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing + Math).
Applicants who are not eligible for assured admission may be reviewed for admission on an individual basis. Individual review takes into consideration academic rigor, extracurricular activities, essays, and other relevant information.

Apply online using ApplyTexas or Common App. Pay the non-refundable $75 application fee. Submit official high school transcript. UNT reviews applications based on a holistic review process that includes academic rigor, essay, extracurricular activities, and test scores (if submitted). Test scores are not required for admission for summer/fall 2024 and spring 2025. If you wish to be considered for admission without SAT/ACT scores, you must submit an essay and resume to be considered.

Applying to UNT for the first time is easy! Submit your application, official transcripts and required test scores. To be considered for direct admission to the College of Engineering, freshman applicants must meet certain high school academic achievement and/or standardized test score requirements. If an applicant does not meet the requirements below, they may apply to UNT as a general university student, and transition to the College of Engineering once they meet transfer admission criteria. Applicants must meet ONE of the following: High School Rank and Test Scores: Top 25%: SAT 1070 (ERW+M) or ACT 21 (Composite); Top 26-50%: SAT 1170 (ERW+M) or ACT 24 (Composite); Top 51-75%: SAT 1270 (ERW+M) or ACT 27 (Composite); No Rank (or international): SAT 1270 (ERW+M) or ACT 27 (Composite). AND High School GPA: 3.0 or higher. AND High School Coursework: Must meet UNT's high school coursework requirements. Test-Optional for Engineering Majors (Fall 2024, Spring 2025, Summer 2025): Applicants who do not meet the test score requirements above, or who choose not to submit test scores, may still be considered for direct admission to the College of Engineering through an individual review process. These applicants must meet the following criteria: High School Rank: Top 25% OR High School GPA: 3.0 or higher. Completion of high school coursework (including Algebra II, Pre-Calculus, Chemistry, and Physics).

To be admitted to the Mechanical Engineering Technology, BS, students must meet the following requirements: Be in good standing with the university. Have completed a minimum of 30 semester hours of college coursework. Have successfully completed the following courses or their approved equivalents with a grade of C or better: MATH 1710, College Algebra or higher level math course; PHYS 1710/1730, General Physics I and Lab; ENGR 2304, Engineering Graphics; ENGR 1030, Introduction to Engineering Technology; TECM 2700, Technical Writing. Have a minimum 2.5 GPA in all courses attempted. Have a minimum 2.5 GPA in all Math, Science, and Engineering Technology courses. International students must meet the university's English language proficiency requirements.
Admission to the College of Music is by audition. For audition dates, requirements and other information, contact the College of Music.

Admission to the College of Music for the Music Education, BM program is by audition only and requires a separate application to the College of Music in addition to application and admission to the University of North Texas. First-year applicants to the University of North Texas must submit a completed application, official high school transcript, and standardized test scores (ACT or SAT). Required materials for the College of Music Undergraduate Application include the College of Music application and a successful audition. A letter of recommendation and scholarship application are optional.

Applicants to the College of Music must satisfy general university admission requirements and be admitted to the university. Applicants must also be accepted into the College of Music after successful audition and satisfactory review of a composition portfolio.

Students must apply and be admitted to the BM in Music: General major. Application is through the College of Music and requires an audition, an interview, and a portfolio. For further information, see the College of Music website or contact the College of Music advising office.

Applicants must submit a completed application for admission to the university, a nonrefundable application fee of $75, an official high school transcript showing class rank and grades, and official ACT or SAT scores. The writing portion of the ACT or SAT is not required. Admission to the College of Music is by entrance audition and competitive examination. All prospective music majors must complete an application for admission to the university and apply for an audition to the College of Music.

Admission to the College of Music is granted to qualified students who have been admitted to the University of North Texas. All students seeking admission to a music degree program must audition, demonstrate musicianship through entrance examinations, and be interviewed by members of the music faculty. All applicants must complete the UNT Admissions application (Apply Texas), be admitted to the University, and complete the College of Music supplemental application (Acceptd). The Acceptd application includes: Contact information, Academic information, Repertoire and performance experience, Audition selections. Optional: Video prescreening for select instruments. Applicants for general university admission are considered based on academic achievement, rigor of curriculum, and standardized test scores (SAT/ACT). UNT is currently test-optional for students applying for Spring 2024, Summer 2024 and Fall 2024 admission. If test scores are not submitted, review will be through an individual holistic review process. Automatic admission for first-time freshmen requires ranking in the top 25% of high school class AND an SAT score of 1030+ (combined Critical Reading and Math) OR an ACT score of 20+ (composite score) OR satisfying the Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP). Theory and Keyboard Entrance Exams are required for Music Majors.

Admission to the College of Visual Arts and Design is a two-fold process. First, students must be admitted to the university, and then to CVAD. All B.F.A. applicants must submit a portfolio including an artist statement and resume/CV. Incoming freshmen and transfer students must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5. Transfer students must have completed at least 12 credit hours.

Students wishing to declare a minor in nonprofit leadership studies must have:
*   Successfully completed 30 semester hours of college coursework;
*   An overall GPA of 2.5 on all college coursework; and
*   A GPA of 2.75 in all courses attempted in the nonprofit leadership studies minor and any courses that are prerequisite to them.
Students must meet the GPA requirements for the business minor.
Program name: Operations and Supply Chain Management (Minor for non-business majors)

Requirements: Students must be in good standing with the university and have a minimum 2.5 GPA at UNT.
Program name: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management (Minor)

Requirements: Students must apply to and be admitted to the university. For assured admission to UNT, students must meet minimum requirements including official documentation of SAT score of 1030 (Evidence-Based Reading & Writing and Math scores combined) or ACT composite score of 20, a high school transcript, and completion of the Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP) high school curriculum requirements or equivalent. Students must be admitted to the CVAD for the BFA in Visual Arts. Students applying for the BFA in Visual Arts must complete a portfolio review and interview. The portfolio review and interview takes place after admission to the university and the completion of foundation courses. Students must have a minimum 2.75 GPA within their foundation courses at UNT to be eligible for portfolio review. Students who transfer foundation courses to UNT must have a minimum 2.75 GPA from the institution where the foundation courses were completed. For the portfolio review, students must submit a portfolio of original works and a letter of intent.

A minor in philosophy is open to all students, regardless of major. It may be declared at any time in consultation with a philosophy advisor. A grade of C or better is required in all courses counted toward the minor.

Admission to the University is required for admission to the college. See general admission requirements for undergraduate programs. A portfolio of work is required for admission to all CVAD studio art programs. See information for admission to the College of Visual Arts and Design.

To declare a minor, a student must contact the academic department in which the minor is offered. A minimum of 18 hours in Physics is required, including: PHYS 1710/1730 or PHYS 1510/1530; PHYS 2220/2240; PHYS 3010 or PHYS 3410; one of PHYS 3310, PHYS 3510, PHYS 4100, PHYS 4110, PHYS 4200, PHYS 4300, PHYS 4310, PHYS 4400, PHYS 4600, PHYS 4700, PHYS 4800, PHYS 4900; and 6 additional advanced hours from PHYS courses (3000-4000 level) for which the student has the prerequisite. A minimum grade of C is required in all courses used to satisfy the minor requirements. At least 9 hours of the minor must be completed at UNT. No more than 6 hours of courses with a grade of D+, D or D- may be counted toward a minor. All minor courses must be passed with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0. A minor may be pursued in any field except the student’s major.

The minor in political science consists of 18 hours, 9 of which must be advanced. A minimum of 6 advanced hours must be completed at UNT. A minimum 2.0 GPA is required in all political science courses counted toward the minor. Students must complete two of the following courses: PSCI 2305, PSCI 2306, PSCI 2300, PSCI 2301, PSCI 2302. Students must complete 12 advanced hours from the courses listed below, or other 3000- or 4000-level PSCI courses with departmental approval. Advanced courses must be taken from at least three of the five subfields below: I. American Government and Politics, II. Public Law, III. Comparative Politics, IV. International Relations, V. Political Theory.

Students interested in pursuing the Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in Art or Design must first be admitted to the university and then to the College of Visual Arts and Design. Admission to the College of Visual Arts and Design for the BFA degree is limited to students who have demonstrated aptitude and potential for professional study in art or design. The college admits qualified students in the following ways:
*   Freshman Admission to the College: Minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA on a 4.0 scale for all high school work; applicants must submit a portfolio of original work in the format and at the time specified by the department; applicants must also submit a statement of intent. No SAT or ACT score is required for freshman admission for the 2024-2025 academic year.
*   Transfer Admission to the College: Minimum 2.75 cumulative GPA for all college work attempted; a minimum of 24 credit hours in art or design with a grade of C or better; applicants must submit a portfolio of original work in the format and at the time specified by the department; applicants must also submit a statement of intent. Transfer students who are Texas residents must meet Texas Success Initiative (TSI) requirements.
*   Current UNT Student Admission to the College: Minimum 2.75 cumulative GPA for all college work attempted; a minimum of 24 credit hours in art or design completed at UNT with a grade of C or better; applicants must submit a portfolio of original work in the format and at the time specified by the department; applicants must also submit a statement of intent.

Applicants must apply to UNT through ApplyTexas or The Common Application. A $75 application fee ($85 for international applicants) is required. Official high school transcripts and official college transcripts for any college-level coursework completed must be submitted. UNT recommends submitting SAT or ACT scores.

A minimum of 18 hours in professional selling, including at least 9 advanced hours. A minimum GPA of 2.0 in courses in the minor. No more than 6 semester hours of professional selling coursework with grades of D+, D or D- may be counted toward the minor. Courses required for the minor cannot be taken Pass/No Pass. Students must complete all required courses in the minor with a minimum grade of C.
Admission to the University of North Texas and to the College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences.

To be admitted to the Public Administration program, students must meet the following requirements: 1. Have completed at least 45 hours of college course work; 2. Have a minimum 2.5 GPA on all college course work attempted; 3. Have completed PSCI 1040 and PSCI 1050 with a grade of C or better; 4. Submit a brief written statement (no more than one page) of your interest in Public Administration to the department for review. This statement should include career goals. The department will approve or deny admission based on the content of the statement.

Admission to the University for First-Time Freshmen requires applicants to meet specific criteria based on high school rank and standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) as outlined in the Assured Admission Standards. Applicants who do not meet assured admission standards but are ranked in the top 50 percent of their high school class may be reviewed individually. Test-optional admission is available for first-time freshmen who meet specific high school rank and GPA criteria (e.g., top 25% rank with a 3.0 GPA) but do not meet minimum SAT/ACT scores for assured admission.

Minimum 18 hours, 9 of which must be advanced (3000/4000 level). Minimum 12 hours must be completed at UNT. Minimum 2.5 UNT GPA in minor courses. A grade of C or better must be earned in all courses counting toward the minor.

Students must meet the following requirements for admission to the Real Estate major: - Be a student in good standing at UNT. - Have a minimum 2.7 cumulative GPA on all work attempted. - Complete 45 hours minimum. - Complete the following courses or their approved equivalents with a minimum grade of C: ADMN 2300, BCIS 2610, ECON 1100, ECON 1110, FINA 3770 (or BCIS 3610), LSCM 3960, MATH 1190 or MATH 1350 or MATH 1400, DSCI 2710 or ITDS 2101, ACCT 2010/2020, BLAW 3430, MRKG 3610. - Completion of all pre-business foundation courses (FINA 3770 is included above but BCIS 3610 is also listed as an option.)
This minor is available only to students not majoring in business.
Admission to the university is subject to the general admission requirements set forth in the catalog.
Program name: Recreation, Event and Sport Management, BS

Requirements: Admission to the program requires: Completion of 30 semester hours with a minimum 2.5 GPA. A minimum 2.5 GPA in all courses attempted at UNT. Completion of ENGL 1310 and ENGL 1320 with a C or better. Completion of MATH 1350 or 1351 or other college-level math with a C or better. An application to the Department of Rehabilitation and Health Services must be submitted and approved by the department.

Admission to the college is based on: 1. A cumulative GPA of 2.7 on a minimum of 30 graded hours of college-level work; 2. Completion of the following courses with a grade of C or better: ECON 1100, ECON 1110, DSCI 2710, MATH 1190 or MATH 1350 or MATH 1400, BCIS 2610 or CSCI 1100, ACCT 2010, ACCT 2020 and BUSI 1200 or BUSI 1201.
A minimum of 18 hours, including 6 advanced hours, from the following courses, with a minimum 2.0 GPA on all courses in the minor.
Program name: Risk Management and Insurance (Minor for non-business majors)

Requirements: A minimum of 18 hours in Russian with at least 12 hours at the advanced level (3000-4000) of which 6 hours must be from UNT. A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 in the minor.

All students seeking a B.A. or B.F.A. degree must meet the general university admission requirements for entering freshmen in addition to meeting the specific entrance requirements for the College of Visual Arts and Design. All undergraduate students (freshman, transfer, change of major) are admitted to the college as Pre-Art majors. Admission to specific professional-level B.F.A. or B.A. studio concentrations (such as Sculpture) occurs after a student has completed specific foundation courses and successfully passed a portfolio review. The portfolio review requires an approved application and acceptance letter, a current unofficial UNT transcript, and 10 pieces of original artwork specific to the area of application.

To be eligible for admission to the BSW Professional Program, students must meet the following requirements:
*   Completion of SCWK 2361 (Introduction to Social Work) with a grade of B or better.
*   Completion of a minimum of 45 semester hours of coursework.
*   A minimum overall GPA of 2.50.
*   A minimum GPA of 2.75 in all Social Work (SCWK) courses.
*   An official degree plan (available from the BSW Program Office) filed with the BSW Program Office.

Students must meet the university requirements for admission to the undergraduate program. Students pursuing a BA in Sociology are encouraged to declare a major in Sociology upon admission to the university, or as soon thereafter as possible. There are no additional requirements for admission to the Sociology major other than those of the university. University undergraduate admission requirements include completing the ApplyTexas Application or Common App, paying the $75 application fee or submitting an application fee waiver, and submitting an official high school transcript.
Students interested in a minor in Spanish should contact the Department of World Languages, Literatures and Cultures to schedule an appointment with an academic advisor.

Admission into the BA with a major in Studio Art does not require a portfolio review. Students interested in the BA with a major in Studio Art should declare the major as soon as possible and take the required foundation courses (ARTT 1440, ARTT 1441, ARTT 1442, ARTT 1443, ARTT 1444 and ARTT 1445).

Students interested in pursuing the BFA in Studio Art are first admitted to the university. After students complete all required Foundation Studies core courses (listed below), they will be eligible to apply for admission to the BFA Studio Art degree program. Admission to the BFA in Studio Art is competitive and based on the quality of a portfolio review and the student’s academic record. Students are encouraged to meet with a CVAD advisor to discuss admission requirements.

Students seeking initial teacher certification must be formally admitted to Teacher Education by application to the College of Education. Admission to Teacher Education requires: 1. Completion of 45 semester hours (sophomore standing). 2. Completion of the course Foundations of Education (EDBE 3000, EDCI 3000, EDSP 3000, or EPSY 3000) with a grade of C or better. 3. A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.75 on all college courses attempted. 4. A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.75 on all university courses attempted. 5. A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.75 on all courses in the major. 6. Official transcripts from all colleges attended outside UNT. 7. Evidence of valid scores on a standardized test of academic skills: Option 1: ACT composite score of 23 or higher. Option 2: SAT composite score of 1130 or higher (Verbal + Math). Option 3: TSIA2 ELAR test score of 945 or higher AND an essay score of 5 or higher OR a TSIA2 ELAR diagnostic score of 5 or higher AND an essay score of 5 or higher. Option 4: TSIA2 Math test score of 950 or higher OR a TSIA2 Math diagnostic score of 6 or higher. Option 5: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution of higher education. 8. Attend a Teacher Education Information Meeting prior to application. 9. Completion of a Statement of Understanding and Compliance. 10. Completion of a criminal history review. 11. Submit a formal application to the College of Education for admission to Teacher Education.
All students must meet the university requirements for general admission as stated in the Admissions section of this catalog.

Students interested in this minor should contact the Department of Dance and Theatre, 940-565-2211, to discuss requirements and to schedule an audition or interview for acceptance into the minor. Auditions and interviews are required for students who wish to emphasize performance in their minor coursework.

Admission to the College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences and the Department of Dance and Theatre. Students must complete an audition/interview to be accepted into the B.A. in Dance, B.A. in Theatre, B.F.A. in Dance, or B.F.A. in Theatre programs. Students accepted into the Design and Technology area must show evidence of practical experience in the area of design and technology, i.e., lighting, scenery, sound, costumes, stage management, etc. Students must interview with Design and Technology faculty and must present a portfolio of work for review. See the Department of Dance and Theatre website for complete information regarding audition and interview requirements.

In addition to fulfilling general university admission requirements, students seeking to major in performance must audition for the faculty of the Department of Dance and Theatre. An audition is required to be accepted as a performance major. Students must make an appointment for an audition. Information on requirements for auditions and scheduling may be found on the department website.

The minor is open to all majors. Students should consult an advisor early in their academic career to assure proper course sequencing and to ensure that the minor is officially declared. Minimum 18 hours, 9 of which must be advanced. A minimum of 6 advanced hours must be completed at UNT. A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.50 in the minor courses at UNT.

Program name: World Languages, Literatures and Cultures, BA
